name: router
description: Path routing beyond svc: typed and wildcard parameters, most-specific matching, 404/405/OPTIONS, path cleaning, trailing slashes, groups, hosts, mounting and reverse URLs

api.name: Segment
api.sig: pub type Segment = Lit{text: Str} | Param{name: Str, kind: Kind} | Rest{name: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: One segment of a compiled pattern: literal text, a parameter of a kind, or the rest of the path.

api.name: Kind
api.sig: pub type Kind = AnyText | Digits | UuidText | Letters | Matching{source: Str, re: Regex} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What a `{name:kind}` parameter accepts: any non-empty segment, decimal digits (a non-negative
`Int`), a UUID in its 8-4-4-4-12 hex form, letters only, or a regular expression that must match
the whole segment.

api.name: Slash
api.sig: pub type Slash = SlashStrict | SlashRedirect | SlashIgnore derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What to do when a path matches a route only with its trailing slash added or removed:
`SlashStrict` answers `404`, `SlashRedirect` redirects to the other form, `SlashIgnore` routes it.

api.name: Options
api.sig: pub type Options = {slash: Slash, clean_paths: Bool, case_insensitive: Bool, auto_options: Bool, auto_head: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
How the table behaves: trailing slashes, redirecting unclean paths (`//`, `.`, `..`) to their
clean form, literal segments compared case-insensitively, `OPTIONS` answered with `Allow`, and
`HEAD` served by `GET` routes.

api.name: Route
api.sig: pub type Route[T] = {methods: List[Str], pattern: Str, host: Str, tags: List[Str], id: T} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A route: the methods it serves (empty for any), its pattern, the host it is limited to (""
for any, `api.example.com`, or `*.example.com` for subdomains), tags for grouping and the id
the router answers with.

api.name: Entry
api.sig: pub type Entry[T] = {route: Route[T], segments: List[Segment]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A compiled route: the route and its parsed segments.

api.name: Table
api.sig: pub type Table[T] = {entries: List[Entry[T]], options: Options} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A compiled routing table.

api.name: Match
api.sig: pub type Match[T] = {id: T, pattern: Str, tags: List[Str], params: List[(Str, Str)]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A route that matched: its id, its pattern, its tags and the decoded parameters in pattern order.

api.name: Resolution
api.sig: pub type Resolution[T] = Matched{found: Match[T]} | Redirected{status: Int, location: Str} | NoRoute | WrongMethod{allow: List[Str]} | OptionsAnswer{allow: List[Str]} | BadPath{why: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Where a request goes: a route, a redirect (to the clean path or the other trailing-slash form),
no route, a route for other methods (with the methods to put in `Allow`), an automatic `OPTIONS`
answer, or a malformed path.

api.name: default_options
api.sig: fn default_options() -> Options
api.doc:
The defaults: redirect between trailing-slash forms and to clean paths, case-sensitive literal
segments, automatic `OPTIONS` and `HEAD`.

api.name: route
api.sig: fn route[T](methods: List[Str], pattern: Str, id: T) -> Route[T]
api.doc:
A route for `methods` (empty for any method) at `pattern`, answering `id`. Methods are
case-sensitive, as RFC 9110 says, so they are written in capitals; `compile` reports others.

api.name: get
api.sig: fn get[T](pattern: Str, id: T) -> Route[T]
api.doc: A `GET` route (also serving `HEAD` when the table's `auto_head` is on).

api.name: post
api.sig: fn post[T](pattern: Str, id: T) -> Route[T]
api.doc: A `POST` route.

api.name: put
api.sig: fn put[T](pattern: Str, id: T) -> Route[T]
api.doc: A `PUT` route.

api.name: patch
api.sig: fn patch[T](pattern: Str, id: T) -> Route[T]
api.doc: A `PATCH` route.

api.name: delete
api.sig: fn delete[T](pattern: Str, id: T) -> Route[T]
api.doc: A `DELETE` route.

api.name: any_method
api.sig: fn any_method[T](pattern: Str, id: T) -> Route[T]
api.doc: A route for every method.

api.name: on_host
api.sig: fn on_host[T](r: Route[T], host: Str) -> Route[T]
api.doc: `r` limited to `host`: an exact host or `*.example.com` for its subdomains.

api.name: tagged
api.sig: fn tagged[T](r: Route[T], tag: Str) -> Route[T]
api.doc: `r` with `tag` added.

api.name: group
api.sig: fn group[T](prefix: Str, tags: List[Str], routes: List[Route[T]]) -> List[Route[T]]
api.doc:
`routes` under `prefix` (`/admin` turns `/users` into `/admin/users` and `/` into `/admin/`),
each tagged with `tags`. Groups nest.

api.name: parse_pattern
api.sig: fn parse_pattern(pattern: Str) -> Res[List[Segment], Str]

api.name: compile
api.sig: fn compile[T](routes: List[Route[T]], opts: Options) -> Res[Table[T], List[Str]]
api.doc:
The table for `routes` under `opts`, or every problem found: bad patterns, bad methods, and
routes that can never be chosen because an earlier route has the same shape, host and an
overlapping method.

api.name: decode_segment
api.sig: fn decode_segment(s: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
`s` with `%XX` escapes decoded (a `+` stays a `+`), or `none` for a bad escape or bytes that are
not UTF-8.

api.name: encode_segment
api.sig: fn encode_segment(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` percent-encoded as one path segment: everything but letters, digits and `-._~!$&'()*+,;=:@`
becomes `%XX`, so a `/` inside a parameter stays inside it.

api.name: kind_accepts
api.sig: fn kind_accepts(k: Kind, s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether the decoded segment `s` is acceptable to `k`.

api.name: clean_path
api.sig: fn clean_path(path: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`path` with empty segments, `.` and `..` removed (never above the root), keeping a trailing
slash, as Go's `path.Clean` does for request paths.

api.name: resolve
api.sig: fn resolve[T](t: Table[T], req: Request) -> Resolution[T]
api.doc: Where `req` goes in `t`. `OPTIONS *` lists every method the table serves.

api.name: answer
api.sig: fn answer[T](r: Resolution[T]) -> Opt[Response]
api.doc:
The response for a resolution that is not a match: `404`, `405` with `Allow`, `204` with
`Allow` for `OPTIONS`, the redirect, or `400`, as RFC 9457 problem details. A match gives `none`.

api.name: route_request
api.sig: fn route_request[T](t: Table[T], req: Request) -> Res[Match[T], Response]
api.doc:
The match for `req`, or the response to send when there is none (see `answer`), for a handler
that dispatches with `match router.route(table, req) | ok(m) => ... | err(r) => r`.

api.name: param
api.sig: fn param[T](m: Match[T], name: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The value of the parameter `name` of `m`.

api.name: param_int
api.sig: fn param_int[T](m: Match[T], name: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The parameter `name` of `m` as an `Int`, or `none` when missing or not a number.

api.name: has_tag
api.sig: fn has_tag[T](m: Match[T], tag: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `m`'s route carries `tag`, for applying a group's middleware.

api.name: allowed_methods
api.sig: fn allowed_methods[T](t: Table[T], path: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc: The methods `t` serves at `path` (what `Allow` would say), empty when no route has the path.

api.name: describe
api.sig: fn describe[T](t: Table[T]) -> List[Str]
api.doc: One line per route, `METHODS pattern [host] -> id`, in table order, for logs and debugging.

api.name: strip_prefix
api.sig: fn strip_prefix(prefix: Str, req: Request) -> Opt[Request]
api.doc:
`req` with `prefix` removed from its path (keeping the query), for passing a request on to a
`svc` or another handler mounted there: `/api/users?x=1` under `/api` is `/users?x=1`, and `/api`
itself is `/`. `none` when the path is not under the prefix.

api.name: url_for
api.sig: fn url_for[T](t: Table[T], id: T, params: List[(Str, Str)], query: List[(Str, Str)]) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The path of the first route in `t` with id `id`, with `params` filled in (each checked against
its kind and percent-encoded; a rest parameter keeps its slashes) and `query` appended. `none`
when there is no such route or a parameter is missing or doesn't fit.
